home.heroEyebrow: European association for the Digital Product Passport
home.introText: DigiPass:Europe is a non-profit technical-scientific association. Its members build, regulate, research and use Digital Product Passports; the association gives them one table, ten working groups and a direct line to the institutions that write the rules.
home.missionTitle: What the statutes ask of us
home.ecosystemTitle: One passport, six kinds of reader
home.ecosystemLead: The passport travels with the product. Every actor along the way writes to it or reads from it; the association exists so that they all agree on how.
benefits: A seat in the working groups
Shape recommendations, guidelines and position papers before they are published.
Monthly tracking of the ESPR, delegated acts and standards, read by the people who must apply them.
Industry, research, technology providers, standards bodies and public authorities in one directory.
Test your implementation against others before a customer or a market-surveillance authority does.
home.wgLead: Members choose their groups; each elects its chair and vice-chair and adopts a yearly work plan.
home.membersTitle: Who is already at the table
home.membersNote: Founding members will be listed here as they are admitted. The profiles shown are illustrative.
calls: Each of the ten working groups elects its leadership among its members.
WG4 and WG10 are forming a cohort of textile companies for a shared pilot.
Members may propose new groups to the Board.
home.ctaTitle: Join the association shaping Europe’s product passports.
home.ctaText: Open to companies of every size, universities, research centres, public bodies and qualified individuals.

about.title: About DigiPass:Europe
about.lead: A non-profit technical-scientific association, founded to be Europe’s networking hub for the Digital Product Passport and the interface to the institutions and standards bodies that define it.
about.objectivesLead: The statutes list the means by which the association pursues its purpose. The working groups and services on this site are how they are put into practice.
about.governanceLead: The bodies of the association are defined in the statutes. Office holders will be published here once elected; no names are listed before then.
about.boardNote: The Board consists of at least five natural persons, the founding members, plus any further members elected by the General Assembly. Names and functions will be published after the constituent meeting.
about.wgLeadershipNote: Each working group elects a chair and a vice-chair. All positions are currently open.
about.statutesText: The Articles of Association (German, with English translation) govern purpose, membership, bodies and dissolution.
about.conditionsLead: Admission and termination follow the statutes.
about.transparencyLead: Non-profit status brings obligations. These are the ones the statutes make binding.
about.reportsText: The Board reports to the General Assembly on the previous year’s activities, submits accounts and prepares the budget. Annual reports will be published here from the first full association year.

membership.title: Membership
membership.lead: Open to companies of every size, universities, research centres, public bodies, technology providers, associations and qualified individuals. Membership categories are those of the statutes; fee levels are proposals for the Board and the General Assembly.
membership.proposedBanner: The fees below are a strategic proposal. They are not adopted prices: the General Assembly sets membership fees and fee categories and the Board assigns each member to a category. The Board may modify this structure at any time.
membership.categoriesLead: Four categories exist. Every tier on this page is a fee level inside one of them.
categories: Authorities, legal entities and other corporations from Austria or abroad. Only the officially named representative votes: 2 to 4 votes depending on fee category.
Persons with a completed relevant education or at least four years of relevant experience. One vote; eligible for the Board.
Students and pupils of higher educational institutions. May attend the General Assembly; no vote.
Recognised experts, and persons honoured for financial support or many years of merit. Honorary members vote and pay no fee.
membership.supporterNote: Supporter is a subscription, not a membership category.
membership.benefitsLead: Benefits are what the association offers; governance rights come from the statutes alone. Sponsorship and partnership never add votes or control.
membership.howLead: The statutes set the procedure. The online application prepares the file; the Board decides.
membership.feesInclude: Fees cover the association year (calendar year); new members pay pro rata by commenced month. Honorary members are exempt.
membership.compare: Download the comparison (PDF) — to be published
membership.questions: Questions about which tier fits? Write to

wg.title: Working groups
wg.lead: The core of the association. Ten groups cover the regulatory, technical, sectoral, economic and human dimensions of the Digital Product Passport. Members may join several groups, stand for chair or vice-chair, and propose new groups to the Board.
wg.membersNote: Member list visible in the member portal once the group is constituted.
wg.joinText: Ordinary members participate fully; extraordinary members may participate in eligible groups. Non-members: start with a membership application.
wg.leadInterest: Express interest in a leadership position
wg.noPubs: No deliverables published yet. Related resources appear in the Knowledge Hub.

activities.title: Activities & projects
activities.lead: Ten programmes give the association’s work a tangible form, and a set of distinctive services goes beyond what a traditional association offers.
activities.extraLead: Services that no comparable European association offers today, prioritised by feasibility and member value. Each is specified so that a development team can start.
activities.projectsText: Research and innovation projects, EU-funded collaborative initiatives and contract work are carried out within the framework of the statutes. The project register will be published here as projects start.
activities.businessText: How the association funds itself, and the limits set by its non-profit status, are described in the business-model note.

join.title: Become a member
join.lead: Eight steps. The first six prepare your application; the Board reviews it as set out in the statutes; payment follows approval.

s1.title: Select your membership category
s1.text: Fees are proposals pending approval by the association’s bodies. The Board assigns the final fee category.

s2.title: Your details
s2.profileHint: Education, experience and current role. For individual membership the Board checks the statutory requirements (relevant degree or ≥ 4 years’ experience).

s3.title: Your organisation
s3.name: Organisation name
s3.vatHint: Required for organisations established in the EU.
s3.representatives: Additional representatives (name and email, one per line)
s3.logoHint: Upload activates once file storage is configured. In demo mode only the file name is recorded.

s4.title: Select working groups
s4.text: Choose the groups you wish to participate in. You can change this later in the member portal.
s4.lead: I am interested in a chair or vice-chair position

s5.title: Conditions
s5.conditions: I accept the membership conditions, including the three-month notice period for resignation.
s5.privacy: I have read the privacy notice and agree to the processing of my data for the membership procedure.
s5.statutes: I acknowledge the Articles of Association and the resolutions of the association’s bodies.

s6.title: Review and submit
s6.text: Check your application. On submission it is forwarded to the Board.

s7.title: Application review
s7.text: The Board deals with the application once two endorsements are on file, one from a Board member. You will be informed of the decision and the fee category in writing. The Board may decline without stating reasons.

s8.title: Payment
s8.text: After approval you receive an invoice for the pro-rata fee of the current association year. Payment by bank transfer; card payment via Stripe once configured.

done.title: Application received
done.demo: Demo mode: this form is fully validated but not connected to a database. Nothing was stored or sent. Once Supabase is configured, applications are saved and the Board is notified by email.
